accepted.question_text: Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g, let L be a fixed determinant line bundle of degree d on C, and let M_{d,r}(C) denote the Fano moduli space of rank-r polystable vector bundles on C with determinant L. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C? In addition, if X_g is the K-moduli space containing the point [M_{d,r}(C)] and X_g has a birational map to the moduli space M_g of smooth genus-g curves, give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of X_g.

evidence.quote:
Problem 9. (1) Show Md,r(C) is K-stable for any smooth projective curve C of genus g.
(2) The K-moduli space Xg containing [Md,r(C)] admits a birational map to Mg, which is
conjecturally isomorphic over Mg by (1). Give a modular interpretation of the limiting
points on X.

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Any smooth Fano threefold X with ρ(X) = 1 is K-semistable.

accepted.question_text: Is every smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety K-stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Any smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety X is K-stable.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Fano variety and T_X its tangent sheaf. Give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable, then T_X is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X. Also give a purely algebraic proof that if T_X is polystable, then there exists a quasi-etale cover f: Y -> X such that Y decomposes as a product of varieties Y = \prod_i X_i and the pulled-back tangent sheaf T_Y = f^*(T_X) decomposes as a direct sum  igoplus_i T_{X_i}, with each T_{X_i} stable with respect to -K_Y.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Fano variety. The class c_1(X) determines a canonical extension 0 -> Omega_X^{[1]} -> E -> O_X -> 0. Give a purely algebraic proof that if X is K-semistable then this extension E is semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X, and that if X is K-polystable then E is polystable with respect to -K_X.

evidence.quote:
Problem 13. Let X be a Fano variety. If X is K-semistable (resp. K-polystable), give an
algebraic proof of the following: the canonical extension E is semistable (resp. polystable) with
respect to the polarization −KX.

accepted.question_text: For a Fano variety X, is the Gibbs-stability invariant gamma(X) > 1 exactly when X is K-stable, and gamma(X) >= 1 exactly when X is K-semistable?

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 15 (Berman). For a Fano variety X, γ(X) > 1 (resp. ≥ 1) if and only if X is
K-stable (resp. K-semistable).

accepted.question_text: Let x in X be a 2n-dimensional symplectic singularity with symplectic form omega_X. If one takes the stable degeneration x_0 in X_0 provided by the normalized-volume theory, is X_0 again symplectic, with a symplectic form omega_{X_0} obtained as a degeneration of omega_X?

evidence.quote:
Problem 20. For a 2n-dimensional symplectic singularity x ∈ X, and any symplectic form ωX,
the stable degeneration x0 ∈ X0 is also symplectic with the symplectic form ωX0 degeneration
of ωX.

accepted.question_text: For the natural contact Fano varieties obtained as projective bases of conical symplectic singularities arising from Lie theory, is the projective base of a nilpotent orbit closure K-polystable? Is the projective base of a Slodowy slice K-polystable?

evidence.quote:
Problem 23. More precisely,
(1) Is the projective base of a nilpotent orbit closure K-polystable?
(2) Is the projective base of a Slodowy slice K-polystable?

accepted.question_text: Let x in X be a symplectic singularity. Is the normalized-volume minimizer always a Kollár component E? If so, must its log discrepancy satisfy A_X(E) = r n for r equal to 1 or 2? After taking the extraction Y -> X of E and the index-one cover of that divisor, does the residue of the pulled-back symplectic form define an orbifold contact structure on E with contact line bundle O_Y(-rE)|_E? Finally, is the resulting log Fano pair underlying E always K-polystable, so that every symplectic singularity admits a Kollár component that is a contact Fano variety in the orbifold sense?
accepted.context_brief: Structure of minimizers for symplectic singularities

accepted.question_text: Let f : (Y, Delta) -> X be a Fano type morphism and let D be a complement. What is the structure of the special valuations LCPS(Y, Delta + D) inside the cone of log-canonical-place valuations LCP(Y, Delta + D)?
accepted.context_brief: Special valuations for Fano type morphisms

evidence.quote:
Problem 35. Let D be a complement of a Fano type morphism f : (Y, ∆) → X. What is the
structure of all special valuations LCPS
(Y, ∆ + D) in LCP(Y, ∆ + D)?

accepted.question_text: Let x in (X = Spec(R), Delta) be a klt singularity, let a_• be an m_x-primary graded sequence of ideals, let c = lct(X, Delta; a_•), and let LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) be the valuations computing that log canonical threshold. Must every valuation in LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) be quasi-monomial? More strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) -> X such that LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) is contained in QM(Y, E) and forms a cone over a connected convex set?
accepted.context_brief: Valuations computing lct of graded ideals

evidence.quote:
Problem 37. In the above notation,
(1) (Weaker version [JM12]) All valuations in LCP(X, ∆ + c · a•) are quasi-monomial.
(2) (Stronger version) There exists a log smooth model (Y, E) → X such that
LCP(X, ∆ + c · a•) ⊆ QM(Y, E)
is a cone over a connected convex set.

accepted.question_text: In the same graded-ideal-sequence setting, does LCP(X, Delta + c a_•) contain a valuation v whose associated graded algebra Gr_v R is finitely generated? More strongly, does it contain a Kollár valuation?

evidence.quote:
Problem 38. In the above notation,
(1) (Weaker version) LCP(X, ∆ +c · a•) contains a valuation v such that the graded algebra
GrvR is finitely generated.
(2) (Stronger version) LCP(X, ∆ + c · a•) contains a Koll´ar valuation.

accepted.question_text: Let x in (X, Delta) be a klt singularity over characteristic 0, and for each sufficiently large prime p let x_p in (X_p, Delta_p) be its reduction modulo p. Is the characteristic-zero normalized volume always the limit of the positive-characteristic Frobenius volumes, namely vol^(x, X, Delta) = lim_{p -> infinity} Fvol(x_p, X_p, Delta_p)?
accepted.context_brief: Reduction mod p and Frobenius volume

accepted.question_text: Let (y in Y) -> (x in X) be a finite morphism that is etale in codimension one. Do the Frobenius volume and Hilbert-Kunz Frobenius volume satisfy the finite-degree formulas Fvol(y, Y) = deg(f) Fvol(x, X) and Fvol_HN(y, Y) = deg(f) Fvol_HN(x, X)?

evidence.quote:
Problem 43. Let (y ∈ Y ) → (x ∈ X) be a finite morphism which is ´etale in codimension one.
We have
Fvol(y, Y ) = deg(f) · Fvol(x, X) and FvolHN(y, Y ) = deg(f) · FvolHN(x, X).

accepted.question_text: Is the Frobenius volume Fvol(x, X) of a singularity always an algebraic number?

evidence.quote: Problem 44. Is Fvol(x, X) an algebraic number?
